title: Workflows vs. agents: who owns control flow

items.stem: In a fixed workflow, what decides which step runs next?

options.text: The model, choosing freely at each step
The code, following steps written in advance
The tool, picking its own next step to run
The user, giving a new instruction before every step

items.stem: In an agent, what decides which tool gets called next?

options.text: The code, following a fixed sequence written in advance
A human operator approving every step live
The model, choosing based on the goal and results so far
The order the tools are listed in the system prompt

items.stem: Name one property of a task that makes a fixed workflow the better choice for keeping its behavior predictable.
Your assistant always searches the manual, extracts the spec, then formats it the same way, in that order. Which control flow fits?

options.text: Workflow — the steps never change, so code can fix them
Agent — the model should pick the first step itself
Agent — calling a tool at all makes it an agent
Workflow — because workflows never call a tool or model

items.stem: A student asks why their 3D print keeps failing. The right next check depends on what earlier checks find, and can't be listed in advance. Which control flow fits?

options.text: Workflow — any question about a manual follows one fixed order
Workflow — it only needs one model call, so it's simple
Agent — it concerns a machine, not because it's predictable
Agent — it picks each check only after seeing the last result

items.stem: In one sentence, why is it easier to predict what a fixed workflow will do on a new input than what an agent will do?
